title: FY25 capital plan: capacity follows demand
preview: Vertex Compute says hyperscaler demand supports a multi-year buildout and outlines a larger capital plan.
article: Vertex Compute raised its capital plan after reporting contracted demand from cloud customers. The filing describes a multi-year buildout, but does not detail the power-delivery schedule for every announced site.
quote: The capital plan follows contracted demand, while power-delivery timing remains a site-level variable.
trustNote: Primary issuer statement; not independent validation.

title: Data-centre connection queue and reserve margin
preview: Public series shows connection requests rising while queue timing and local reserve data remain incomplete.
article: The public series records rising connection requests alongside a tighter reserve margin in several planning zones. It is a useful baseline, but the lag means it cannot resolve the full 2028 operating-capacity question.
quote: Connection requests are rising, but the public series does not yet resolve when queued capacity can energise.
trustNote: Open primary dataset; lagged and incomplete for 2028.

title: Why the next campus is already spoken for
preview: An industry blog repeats the company-capex narrative and frames demand as the binding constraint.
article: Buildout Weekly argues that demand is the binding constraint for the next wave of campuses. Its examples closely follow company announcements and add limited independent delivery evidence.
quote: The next campus is already spoken for, according to the same demand announcements circulated by issuers.
trustNote: Derivative commentary; overlaps Vertex Compute.

title: Suppliers feel the pull of the AI buildout
preview: Supplier interviews point to strong near-term demand, but transformer and switchgear lead times are stretching.
article: Two equipment suppliers describe a durable order book for AI infrastructure, but warn that transformers and switchgear are being booked well ahead of delivery. The reporting adds an independent check on issuer-led demand claims.
quote: Two switchgear suppliers said booked orders now extend beyond twelve months, even as accelerator demand remains firm.
trustNote: Independent wire reporting with supplier comments.

title: AI campuses: the equipment squeeze
preview: A short newsletter echoes Northstar’s supplier bottleneck framing with little additional sourcing.
article: Circuit Note repeats the equipment bottleneck story and cites the same supplier comments already used in Northstar Wire. The article is useful as a duplication check, not as a second independent family.
quote: Equipment vendors are busy and delivery windows are longer; the note cites the same public supplier comments circulated in the wire market.
trustNote: Heavily overlaps Northstar Wire; no independent family added.

title: Grid connections, not chips, set the pace
preview: Interviews with grid operators and developers complicate the buildout story: interconnection studies, not chips, set the pace in constrained markets.
article: Grid operators and developers describe a widening gap between signed connection agreements and energisation. The report argues that interconnection studies, substation work, and queue position can add years to an otherwise funded campus.
quote: A signed connection agreement is not the same as energisation; studies, substation work, and queue position can add years.
trustNote: Independent report with operator and developer interviews.

title: The interconnection queue will decide 2028
preview: A specialist report offers regional queue benchmarks and project-level interconnection lead times.
article: GridScope Asia assembles regional queue benchmarks and project-level timelines for constrained Asian hubs. It is the most detailed source in the set, but its quote exceeds the S$1.00 per-source mandate ceiling.
quote: The specialist dataset estimates 18–36 months from a complete interconnection application to a firm energisation window in the most constrained Asian hubs.
trustNote: High-value specialist source; above the S$1 auto-buy ceiling.

title: Accelerator supply normalises, with packaging caveats
preview: Packaging capacity has improved, though advanced assembly remains a watch point for delivery schedules.
article: The index shows accelerator supply normalising while advanced packaging remains a watch point. It provides component context without resolving project-level grid delivery.
quote: Packaging capacity has improved, though advanced assembly remains a watch point for delivery schedules.
trustNote: Open industry series; context, not a capacity forecast.

title: Cooling is becoming a site-selection constraint
preview: A technical review describes cooling and water requirements that can delay dense AI campuses.
article: Technical operators report that cooling and water requirements are reshaping site selection for dense AI campuses. The review is relevant context, but it carries no project-level delivery evidence.
quote: Cooling and water requirements can delay a dense campus even when compute equipment is available.
trustNote: Technical context with no project-level delivery data.

title: Funding the second wave of compute
preview: Debt markets remain open for strong sponsors, but construction financing is sensitive to timing and utilisation.
article: Credit remains available to strong sponsors, although construction financing is increasingly sensitive to delivery timing and expected utilisation. The note links financing risk to operations rather than demand alone.
quote: Construction financing is sensitive to timing and utilisation, not only to the size of the announced pipeline.
trustNote: Independent market commentary; no operating-capacity evidence.

title: Specialty construction labour remains tight
preview: A public index shows specialist electrical and commissioning labour shortages across major hubs.
article: The public index shows persistent shortages in specialist electrical and commissioning labour. Geography is broad, so it is a leading indicator rather than a project forecast.
quote: Specialist electrical and commissioning labour remains tight across the major buildout hubs.
trustNote: Open primary index; geography is broad.

title: AI capex: the trillion-dollar runway
preview: A market digest compiles public company announcements and repeats the demand thesis.
article: Market Signal Digest compiles public company announcements into a bullish runway narrative. It is a useful discovery lead but adds no independent evidence family.
quote: The runway looks large because the digest aggregates the same public announcements across issuers.
trustNote: Derivative compilation; adds no independent evidence.

title: Long bonds absorb a fiscal and inflation shock
preview: A sharp move in long yields reflects a mix of fiscal supply, sticky inflation risk, and crowded duration positioning.
article: Long-duration government bonds sold off as investors repriced fiscal supply and the persistence of inflation. Dealers described the move as a positioning shock amplified by thin liquidity rather than a single-data-point reaction.
quote: The selloff combined fiscal supply, sticky inflation risk, and crowded duration positioning in a thin market.
trustNote: Synthetic wire fixture; combines market and dealer observations.

title: The term premium is doing more of the work
preview: Models suggest the long-end move is increasingly explained by term premium, not only expected policy rates.
article: A term-premium decomposition attributes much of the long-end move to compensation for duration risk. The report cautions that the estimate is model-dependent, but it narrows the debate beyond a simple central-bank narrative.
quote: The long-end repricing is increasingly a term-premium story, not only a forecast for the next policy meeting.
trustNote: Synthetic specialist research with an explicit model caveat.

title: Supply calendars are heavier at the long end
preview: The auction calendar shows a greater share of issuance arriving in maturities most sensitive to duration demand.
article: The public auction calendar shows a heavier long-end issuance profile over the next two quarters. It establishes supply pressure, but not how dealers or real-money investors will absorb it.
quote: The issuance calendar is heavier where duration demand is most sensitive to price.
trustNote: Open fixture data; no investor-positioning read-through.

title: Officials are less willing to cushion inflation surprises
preview: Recent minutes show less willingness to pre-commit to cuts while inflation expectations remain uneven.
article: Recent policy minutes show officials resisting a pre-commitment to cuts while inflation expectations remain uneven. That raises the sensitivity of the bond market to incoming inflation and labour data.
quote: Officials are leaving the path open, which makes each inflation surprise more consequential for duration pricing.
trustNote: Public fixture summary of primary-policy language.

title: Credit has not confirmed a full risk-off break
preview: Corporate spreads remain contained even as government duration sells off, making the episode look more like a rates shock than a broad credit event.
article: Investment-grade spreads have widened only modestly while government yields rose sharply. The divergence argues against describing the move as a generalized credit panic, although leveraged borrowers remain exposed to higher refinancing costs.
quote: Contained credit spreads make this look more like a rates shock than a full credit liquidation.
trustNote: Synthetic market fixture; separates rates and credit stress.

title: Crowded duration makes the exit nonlinear
preview: Positioning surveys show duration exposure concentrated among investors who may need liquidity at the same time.
article: Positioning data indicates that duration exposure is concentrated among investors with similar liquidity windows. The note does not establish the size of the trade, but it explains why small yield changes can trigger outsized price moves.
quote: Concentrated duration exposure can turn a modest yield repricing into a nonlinear exit.
trustNote: Open fixture survey; positioning is directional, not a full flow record.

title: Weak tail bids point to a demand problem at the margin
preview: Recent auction tails suggest marginal demand is less price-insensitive than it was earlier in the cycle.
article: Auction tails widened at the long end, with indirect demand less consistent than in prior months. The report treats this as evidence about marginal absorption, not proof that the market has lost a structural buyer base.
quote: Long-end auction tails widened, signalling that marginal demand is becoming more price-sensitive.
trustNote: Synthetic specialist fixture; marginal-demand evidence only.

title: Real yields, not breakevens, lead the move
preview: The move is concentrated in real yields, suggesting growth and supply expectations matter alongside inflation compensation.
article: A real-yield decomposition shows the largest move in inflation-adjusted yields rather than breakevens. That points to real-rate and supply expectations as an important part of the repricing, but the article is priced above the mandate ceiling.
quote: Real yields led breakevens, so the move cannot be explained by inflation compensation alone.
trustNote: High-value fixture analysis; blocked above the mandate ceiling.
